source.excerpt: No one ever made a decision because of a number.
trail: Wikiquote cites Michael Lewis’s The Undoing Project (2016), rather than a book authored by Kahneman.
The inspected November 2019 De Psycholoog article reproduces the two sentences and a continuation, crediting Kahneman in Lewis (2016), p. 250.
This supports the reported attribution. It does not establish when or where Kahneman first said it, nor prove the literal universal claim about all decisions.

author.name: Daniel Kahneman
author.heading: About Daniel Kahneman
author.bio: Daniel Kahneman (1934–2024) was an Israeli-American psychologist associated with Princeton University. His work with Amos Tversky helped explain systematic patterns in judgment and decision-making; he received the 2002 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences and brought this research to a broad readership in Thinking, Fast and Slow.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The saying contrasts numerical probabilities with the narratives people use to understand choices. Its source trail is Michael Lewis’s account of Kahneman, and a later psychology article uses it when discussing professional judgment in selection decisions. That transmission matters: it is reported speech rather than a maxim located in Kahneman’s own Thinking, Fast and Slow.
